text: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks. We propose the Transformer, a new simple network architecture based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.

The Transformer uses multi-head self-attention with eight parallel attention heads. Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions, which a single attention head averages away.

Since the model contains no recurrence and no convolution, we inject positional encoding using sine and cosine functions of different frequencies so that the model can make use of the order of the sequence.

On the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task the big Transformer model achieves 28.4 BLEU, improving over the existing best results including ensembles by more than two BLEU points while training substantially faster.

We introduce BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. BERT is designed to pretrain deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.

We pretrain BERT using two unsupervised tasks: the masked language model objective, which randomly masks tokens and predicts them from context, and next sentence prediction, which teaches the model relationships between sentence pairs.
BERT obtains new state of the art results on eleven natural language processing tasks, including pushing the GLUE score to 80.5 percent and SQuAD v1.1 question answering test F1 to 93.2.

We explore retrieval augmented generation, a general purpose fine tuning recipe that combines pretrained parametric memory with a non parametric memory consisting of a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed with a neural retriever.
The retriever is a dense passage retriever that encodes the query and documents into a shared embedding space, and the generator is a sequence to sequence model conditioned on the retrieved passages.

Retrieval augmented generation still struggles with queries that require aggregating information across many documents, because the retriever selects a small number of passages independently and cannot reason over global structure.

We present GraphRAG, a graph based approach to query focused summarization that builds an entity knowledge graph from source documents and pregenerates community summaries for groups of closely related entities.

Baseline retrieval augmented generation performs poorly on global sensemaking questions such as what are the main themes in this corpus, because such questions are not answerable by retrieving a handful of locally similar text chunks.

The indexing pipeline extracts entities and relationships with a large language model, detects communities using the Leiden algorithm, and generates a summary for each community at multiple levels of the hierarchy.

Across two corpora of about one million tokens, graph based summarization substantially improved comprehensiveness and diversity of answers over a naive retrieval augmented generation baseline as judged by a language model evaluator.

We propose Low Rank Adaptation, or LoRA, which freezes the pretrained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture, greatly reducing the number of trainable parameters for downstream tasks.

LoRA reduces the number of trainable parameters by ten thousand times and the GPU memory requirement by three times compared with full fine tuning of GPT-3 175B, while performing on par or better in model quality.
